en.greeting: Hi! Today we go travelling: the airport, the hotel, tickets, how to describe a route, and what you do on holiday.

steps.title: At the airport
steps.text: Let's start at Soekarno-Hatta Airport. Here are the words you see and hear there.
steps.body: You **check in** at the check-in desk: you give them your **luggage** and get a **boarding pass**. Then you go to your **gate**. **Luggage / baggage** can't be counted, like rice: no *a*, no *-s* (*two bags*, not 'two luggages'). Trap: Indonesians say 'pesawatnya delay', but in English it's **The flight is delayed** or **There's a delay**.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Bad news on the airport screen.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Penerbangan kami ke Lombok ditunda.
question.solution: Our flight to Lombok is delayed.
question.explanation: Ditunda = **is delayed**: English needs **is** and the **-ed** form, not 'is delay'. Order: who or what (**Our flight to Lombok**) + **is delayed**.

steps.title: Hotels and tickets
steps.text: Now you arrive at your hotel. And you need tickets for the train or the boat.
steps.body: **Book** is also a verb: **book a room** = memesan kamar. A **single room** is for one person, a **double room** for two (one big bed). **Reception** is the desk; the person is the **receptionist**. **Check in** when you arrive, **check out** when you leave and pay. Tickets: **one-way** = sekali jalan, **return** = pulang-pergi. British vs American: return ticket (UK) = **round-trip ticket** (US).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina is at Gambir station.

question.prompt: Rina has a new job in Surabaya. She needs a train ticket to Surabaya, and she doesn't come back to Jakarta. What does she say at the ticket office?
options: A return ticket to Surabaya, please.
A back ticket to Surabaya, please.
A one-way ticket to Surabaya, please.
question.explanation: She only goes there, so she needs a **one-way ticket** (sekali jalan). A **return ticket** is there and back (pulang-pergi), and 'back ticket' isn't English.

steps.title: Into, across, along, past
steps.text: Now let's describe a route. These little words say where you move.
steps.body: They come after a moving verb (go, walk, drive): **into** = masuk ke dalam, **out of** = keluar dari, **across** = dari satu sisi ke sisi lain, **along** = menyusuri (a road, a river, a beach), **past** = melewati, without stopping. Trap: **pass** and **past** sound almost the same. After walk / go / drive it's **past**: *walk past*, never 'walk pass'.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A tourist asks you the way to the hotel.

question.prompt: The hotel is after the bank, on the same side of the road. Don't stop at the bank. Complete: Walk ___ the bank. The hotel is on the right.
options: across
pass
past
question.explanation: You go by the bank without stopping: **walk past** (melewati). 'Pass' sounds the same but is a verb on its own, so 'walk pass' is wrong. **Across** means to the other side, but the hotel is on the same side.

steps.title: Get on the bus, get into the taxi
steps.text: Indonesian says naik and turun for every vehicle. English has two pairs.
steps.body: **get on / get off**: bus, train, plane, boat, motorbike (big, or you sit on top). **get into / get out of**: car, taxi (small, you bend down and sit inside). Not 'We go into the bus' but **We get on the bus**. A1 **by bus** is how you travel; **get on the bus** is the moment you step in.

examples.en: The bus is here. Let's get on!
We get off the plane at Ngurah Rai Airport.
examples.id: Kami turun dari pesawat di Bandara Ngurah Rai.

examples.en: The ojek is here. I get on the motorbike.
examples.id: Ojeknya sudah datang. Saya naik ke motornya.

examples.en: Sari gets out of the taxi at the hotel.
examples.id: Sari turun dari taksi di hotel.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas takes the KRL home from work.

question.prompt: Dimas lives in Bogor. The train stops at Bogor station and the doors open. Dimas ___ the train.
options: gets on
gets off
goes off
question.explanation: He's home, so he leaves the train: **gets off** (turun). A train is big, so it's **on / off**. **Gets on** is when you go in, and 'goes off' isn't used for leaving a train.

steps.title: On holiday
steps.text: Last part: what do you do on holiday?
steps.body: Pergi liburan = **go on holiday**, never 'go to holiday': holiday isn't a place. A place takes **to**: *go to Lombok*. Activities use go + **-ing**: *go sightseeing, go snorkelling*. Ambil foto = **take photos**, not 'make photos'. British vs American: holiday (UK) = **vacation** (US); snorkelling (UK) = **snorkeling** (US).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Bu Ani talks about her parents.

options: My parents go to holiday in Bali every August.
My parents go holiday in Bali every August.
My parents go on holiday to Bali every August.
question.explanation: Pergi liburan = **go on holiday**, and the place takes **to**: *go on holiday to Bali*. 'Go to holiday' treats holiday like a place, and 'go holiday' is missing *on*.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Take it on your next trip!

**Walk past** the bank, not 'walk pass'. **Get on** the bus, **get into** the taxi.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? Try these exercises on hotel and holiday words.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita jalan-jalan: bandara, hotel, tiket, cara menjelaskan rute, dan kegiatan saat liburan.

steps.title: Di bandara
steps.text: Kita mulai di Bandara Soekarno-Hatta. Ini kata-kata yang kamu lihat dan dengar di sana.
steps.body: Kamu **check in** di meja check-in: kamu menyerahkan **luggage** (bagasi) dan mendapat **boarding pass**. Lalu kamu pergi ke **gate**. **Luggage / baggage** tidak bisa dihitung, seperti rice: tanpa *a*, tanpa *-s* (*two bags*, bukan 'two luggages'). Jebakan: kita bilang 'pesawatnya delay', tapi dalam bahasa Inggris **The flight is delayed** atau **There's a delay**.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Kabar buruk di layar bandara.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Penerbangan kami ke Lombok ditunda.
question.solution: Our flight to Lombok is delayed.
question.explanation: Ditunda = **is delayed**: bahasa Inggris perlu **is** dan bentuk **-ed**, bukan 'is delay'. Urutannya: siapa atau apa (**Our flight to Lombok**) + **is delayed**.

steps.title: Hotel dan tiket
steps.text: Sekarang kamu tiba di hotel. Kamu juga perlu tiket kereta atau kapal.
steps.body: **Book** juga kata kerja: **book a room** = memesan kamar. **Single room** untuk satu orang, **double room** untuk dua orang (satu ranjang besar). **Reception** adalah mejanya; orangnya **receptionist**. **Check in** saat datang, **check out** saat pergi dan membayar. Tiket: **one-way** = sekali jalan, **return** = pulang-pergi. Inggris (UK) vs Amerika (US): return ticket (UK) = **round-trip ticket** (US).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina ada di Stasiun Gambir.

question.prompt: Rina dapat pekerjaan baru di Surabaya. Dia perlu tiket kereta ke Surabaya, dan dia tidak kembali ke Jakarta. Apa yang dia katakan di loket tiket?
options: A return ticket to Surabaya, please.
A back ticket to Surabaya, please.
A one-way ticket to Surabaya, please.
question.explanation: Dia hanya pergi ke sana, jadi dia perlu **one-way ticket** (sekali jalan). **Return ticket** itu pergi dan pulang (pulang-pergi), dan 'back ticket' bukan bahasa Inggris.

steps.title: Into, across, along, past
steps.text: Sekarang kita jelaskan rute. Kata-kata kecil ini menunjukkan ke mana kamu bergerak.
steps.body: Letaknya setelah kata kerja gerak (go, walk, drive): **into** = masuk ke dalam, **out of** = keluar dari, **across** = dari satu sisi ke sisi lain, **along** = menyusuri (jalan, sungai, pantai), **past** = melewati, tanpa berhenti. Jebakan: **pass** dan **past** bunyinya hampir sama. Setelah walk / go / drive pakai **past**: *walk past*, jangan 'walk pass'.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Seorang turis menanyakan jalan ke hotel.

question.prompt: Hotelnya setelah bank, di sisi jalan yang sama. Jangan berhenti di bank. Lengkapi: Walk ___ the bank. The hotel is on the right.
options: across
pass
past
question.explanation: Kamu lewat bank tanpa berhenti: **walk past** (melewati). 'Pass' bunyinya sama tapi itu kata kerja yang berdiri sendiri, jadi 'walk pass' salah. **Across** artinya ke seberang, padahal hotelnya di sisi yang sama.

steps.title: Naik bus, masuk ke taksi
steps.text: Bahasa Indonesia memakai naik dan turun untuk semua kendaraan. Bahasa Inggris punya dua pasang.
steps.body: **get on / get off**: bus, kereta, pesawat, kapal, motor (besar, atau kamu duduk di atasnya). **get into / get out of**: mobil, taksi (kecil, kamu membungkuk lalu duduk di dalam). Bukan 'We go into the bus' tapi **We get on the bus**. **By bus** dari A1 adalah cara bepergian; **get on the bus** adalah saat kamu melangkah masuk.

examples.en: The bus is here. Let's get on!
We get off the plane at Ngurah Rai Airport.
examples.id: Kami turun dari pesawat di Bandara Ngurah Rai.

examples.en: The ojek is here. I get on the motorbike.
examples.id: Ojeknya sudah datang. Saya naik ke motornya.

examples.en: Sari gets out of the taxi at the hotel.
examples.id: Sari turun dari taksi di hotel.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas pulang kerja naik KRL.

question.prompt: Dimas tinggal di Bogor. Keretanya berhenti di Stasiun Bogor dan pintunya terbuka. Lengkapi: Dimas ___ the train.
options: gets on
gets off
goes off
question.explanation: Dia sudah sampai, jadi dia keluar dari kereta: **gets off** (turun). Kereta itu besar, jadi pakai **on / off**. **Gets on** saat naik, dan 'goes off' tidak dipakai untuk turun dari kereta.

steps.title: Saat liburan
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: apa yang kamu lakukan saat liburan?
steps.body: Pergi liburan = **go on holiday**, jangan 'go to holiday': holiday bukan tempat. Tempat memakai **to**: *go to Lombok*. Kegiatan memakai go + **-ing**: *go sightseeing, go snorkelling*. Ambil foto = **take photos**, bukan 'make photos'. Inggris (UK) vs Amerika (US): holiday (UK) = **vacation** (US); snorkelling (UK) = **snorkeling** (US).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bu Ani bercerita tentang orang tuanya.

options: My parents go to holiday in Bali every August.
My parents go holiday in Bali every August.
My parents go on holiday to Bali every August.
question.explanation: Pergi liburan = **go on holiday**, dan tempatnya memakai **to**: *go on holiday to Bali*. 'Go to holiday' menganggap holiday sebagai tempat, dan 'go holiday' kurang *on*.
